clinical_history.summary: 58-year-old man with three weeks of progressive fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, gingival bleeding, and scattered lower-extremity ecchymoses. Peripheral smear with 41% circulating blasts, some with folded nuclei and abundant cytoplasm. No prior hematologic history, no prior chemotherapy or radiation. Bone marrow performed to evaluate for acute leukemia.

morphology.blast_count_method: 500-cell manual aspirate differential; promonocytes (4%) enumerated separately from blasts
morphology.core_blast_assessment: Markedly hypercellular core with extensive replacement by immature mononuclear cells arranged in sheets; interstitial and paratrabecular distribution; extensive blast-equivalent infiltration
morphology.lineage_assessment: Myeloid process with probable monocytic differentiation by morphology and cytochemistry; to be confirmed by flow cytometry. Occasional monocytoid cells noted, but unequivocal promonocytes are difficult to distinguish from immature myeloid forms on morphology alone.
morphology.auer_rods: No definite Auer rods identified after review of multiple smears

cytochemistry.result: positive in a minor subset of blasts (approximately 5-10%)
positive in a subset of cells with partial fluoride inhibition, supporting a monocytic component
storage iron present; no ring sideroblasts

morphology.dysplasia_notes: Erythropoiesis is left-shifted with mild megaloblastoid change. Megakaryocytes are reduced (markedly reduced on core). No ring sideroblasts.
morphology.morphologic_diagnosis: HYPERCELLULAR MARROW WITH ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA (see comment). Aspirate blast count 18% by 500-cell manual differential; core biopsy with extensive blast-equivalent infiltration. Probable monocytic differentiation by morphology and cytochemistry; to be confirmed by flow cytometry.
morphology.stated_limitations: Manual aspirate blast percentage (18%) is below the historical 20% threshold; aspirate enumeration is likely affected by hemodilution and by the difficulty of separating promonocytes from myeloid blasts on smears. Classification depends on integration with flow cytometry, cytogenetic, and molecular results, pending at time of report. Component report not intended to stand alone.

molecular.panel_description: Myeloid neoplasm next-generation sequencing panel (54-gene), hybrid-capture targeted NGS on genomic DNA from bone marrow; mean target coverage 1,150x, minimum 250x; FLT3-ITD detection supplemented by capillary fragment analysis.

variants_detected.hgvs: Internal tandem duplication, exon 14 (~36 bp insertion)
variants_detected.prognostic_note: Report states FLT3-ITD is prognostically adverse and a target for FLT3 inhibitor therapy; allelic ratio 0.62 reported to support treatment decisions.

Report states commonly co-mutated with NPM1 and FLT3-ITD, frequently a clonal hematopoiesis founder event; does not by itself define or change the WHO/ICC disease category; reported for completeness and potential prognostic relevance.

molecular.molecular_interpretation: Mutated NPM1 (type A, VAF 39%) with FLT3-ITD (VAF 31%, allelic ratio 0.62) and DNMT3A R882H (VAF 44%). The report states that, in the context of AML established by morphology and flow cytometry, mutated NPM1 is a WHO and ICC disease-defining genetic abnormality and that a 20% blast threshold is not required for this entity. FLT3-ITD is prognostically adverse and targetable. DNMT3A R882H does not by itself define or change the disease category.
molecular.stated_limitations: Analytical sensitivity approximately 5% VAF for SNVs and small indels. Does not reliably detect large structural rearrangements, copy-number changes, or variants in regions of low coverage or high homology. A negative result does not exclude a mutation below the limit of detection. Laboratory-developed test, not FDA cleared or approved.

concordances.statement: All four reports share the same patient (DOE, JONATHAN R.), MRN (MRN-4471902), DOB (1967-09-14), and collection date (2026-04-22); the molecular report also cross-references client accession S26-BM-01187 and the cytogenetics report references MMD-26-NGS-22150.
Identical clinical history and CBC (WBC 38.4 x10^9/L, Hb 7.9 g/dL, platelets 31 x10^9/L, 41% peripheral blasts) repeated in all four reports.
Morphology and flow cytometry both identify acute myeloid leukemia with monocytic differentiation (probable on morphology/cytochemistry, established on flow).
MPO is expressed in only a subset of blasts by both cytochemistry (approximately 5-10%) and flow (positive, dim subset).

Morphology (folded/indented nuclei, monocytoid features, NSE positivity) and flow (expanded monocytic compartment) both support a monocytic component; peripheral blasts with folded nuclei noted in shared history.
Morphology and molecular reports both state that under WHO/ICC a 20% blast count is not required when a defining genetic abnormality is present.

Cytogenetics finds no recurrent AML abnormality and no TP53 deletion; molecular finds no TP53, RUNX1, or KIT variant and identifies gene-level drivers, consistent with the cytogenetics report's statement that cytogenetically normal AML is frequently driven by gene-level mutations.
All four reports state that final classification requires integration of the component studies.

positions.position: Aspirate blast count 18% by 500-cell manual differential (promonocytes 4% counted separately); core shows extensive blast-equivalent infiltration.
Myeloid blasts approximately 22% of total nucleated cells by CD45/SSC gating; promonocytes/immature monocytic 11% counted with monocytic series.

discordances.resolution: Both values are recorded as reported; the difference is expected methodological variance and does not need to be forced to a single number at this stage.
discordances.resolution_basis: Manual smear differentials and gated flow counts are expected to differ (stated by FLOW); MORPH attributes its lower count to hemodilution of the aspirate and difficulty separating promonocytes from myeloid blasts; the core biopsy shows infiltration well above either figure. Both MORPH and MOLEC state that a 20% blast threshold is not required when a defining genetic abnormality is present, and MOLEC reports mutated NPM1, so the 18% vs 22% straddling of 20% is not decisive.

positions.position: Probable monocytic differentiation by morphology and cytochemistry; to be confirmed by flow cytometry; promonocytes hard to separate from immature myeloid forms.
Diagnostic of AML with monocytic differentiation; immunophenotype establishes the monocytic lineage.

discordances.resolution: Not a true conflict: morphology hedges and explicitly defers to flow; flow confirms monocytic lineage.
discordances.resolution_basis: Immunophenotyping (bright uniform CD64, CD14, CD11b, CD11c, CD36, dim CD4 on an expanded monocytic compartment) is the more specific method for monocytic lineage assignment; MORPH itself states its call is to be confirmed by flow cytometry.

discordances.topic: Aspirate morphologic diagnosis below historical 20% blast threshold vs AML diagnosis

positions.position: Manual aspirate blast percentage (18%) is below the historical 20% threshold, yet AML is diagnosed with comment.
Mutated NPM1 is a WHO/ICC disease-defining abnormality; a blast threshold of 20% is not required for this entity.

discordances.resolution: The apparent tension is resolved by the stated classification rule reported in both MORPH and MOLEC; final classification left to Stage 2.
discordances.resolution_basis: Classification rule as stated in the source reports: under WHO and ICC, AML with a defining genetic abnormality (mutated NPM1, reported by MOLEC) does not require a 20% blast count.

single_source_findings.finding: NPM1 type A frameshift insertion (c.860_863dup), VAF 39% - the disease-defining genetic abnormality
single_source_findings.diagnostic_impact: Per MOLEC, defines the WHO/ICC disease category and removes the 20% blast requirement, rendering the 18% vs 22% blast discordance non-decisive. Karyotype and FISH were normal, and morphology/flow cannot detect gene-level mutations.

single_source_findings.finding: FLT3 internal tandem duplication, VAF 31%, ITD/WT allelic ratio 0.62
single_source_findings.diagnostic_impact: Does not change disease category but is prognostically adverse and identifies a target for FLT3 inhibitor therapy; directly affects risk stratification and treatment.

single_source_findings.finding: DNMT3A R882H, VAF 44% (possible clonal hematopoiesis founder event)
single_source_findings.diagnostic_impact: Non-classifying; potential prognostic relevance only. Must not drift into the classification.

single_source_findings.finding: Aberrant CD56 (partial) and CD7 (subset) expression on blasts
single_source_findings.diagnostic_impact: No change to diagnosis; provides a leukemia-associated immunophenotype useful for measurable residual disease tracking.

single_source_findings.finding: Normal karyotype 46,XY[20] with negative AML FISH panel (excludes recurrent rearrangements including PML-RARA, RUNX1-RUNX1T1, CBFB, KMT2A, MECOM, and -5/-7/17p loss)
single_source_findings.diagnostic_impact: Excludes competing cytogenetically defined AML entities and adverse-risk cytogenetic lesions; MOLEC states its assay does not reliably detect large structural rearrangements or copy-number changes, so only CYTO can exclude these.
